Called by Committee Chair

  SPECIAL – BUDGET AND FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE (BFAC) MEETING

  Friday, September 11, 2026

  ROOM 401, CITY HALL - 12:30 PM
  200 NORTH SPRING STREET, LOS ANGELES, CA 90012

  MEMBERS:  RON S. GALPERIN, CHAIR
  DERRIC J. JOHNSON, VICE CHAIR
  GILDA HAAS
  JOSEPH M. LUMARDA
  TOM DE SIMONE

  Armando Bencomo - Legislative Assistant - (213) 978-1080
  (or Clerk.BudgetandFinanceCommittee@lacity.org)

  Submit written comment at LACouncilComment.com

The audio for Committee meetings is broadcast live on the internet at https://clerk.lacity.gov/calendar.

The Committee will take public comment from members of the public in-person only; there will be no public comment by
teleconference. Additional information regarding Committee procedures provided at the end of this agenda.

For interpretation services and Sign Language Interpreters, at no cost, please contact clerk.interpretation@lacity.org or call (213)
978-1133 and provide the language desired, specific meeting, meeting date, and the number of people in the group.

All requests should be submitted with as much advance notice as possible, preferably two business days prior to the meeting you
wish to attend for additional language interpretation and five business days for Sign Language Interpretation. We will do our best to
accommodate requests with shorter notice, but securing last-minute interpreters or captioners may not always be feasible.

ITEM(S)

 (1)  Call to Order and Roll Call

 (2)  Public Comment

  • Multiple Agenda Item Comment
  (3)  City Asset Management Presentation
  Invited speakers from SOMOS Group will present recommendations
  for the management and development of City-owned land.

 (4)  Staff Update
  Staff will share recent stakeholder engagement efforts and relevant
  City-wide policies.

 (5)  Policy Area Deliberation
  Committee members will deliberate and adopt a set of policy areas to
  move forward with crafting recommendations.

 (6)  Approval of Minutes
  The Committee will review and approve the Minutes of the July 10,
  2026, Budget and Finance Advisory Committee meeting.

 (7)  Next Steps and Calendar Review

 (8)  Adjournment

SUPPORTING MATERIALS

Materials relating to items on the agenda are available on the Budget and Finance Advisory Committee webpage found at
https://councilcommittee.lacity.gov/budget/BudgetandFinanceAdvisory/. To subscribe to the Budget and Finance Advisory Committee
agendas, please subscribe using this link: https://lacity.gov/government/subscribe-agendas/city-council

PUBLIC INPUT AT CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE MEETINGS

Members of the public who wish to speak on one or multiple items shall have an opportunity to speak up to one minute per item up
to a total of two minutes for two or more agenda items. At regular meetings, members of the public shall also have an opportunity to
speak up to one minute for general public comment on any matter within the subject-matter jurisdiction of the Committee. The
Committee is not required to take general public comment at special meetings. The Committee may limit the total amount of time for
public comment on any specific agenda item, on all agenda-items collectively, and/or on general public comment, based on the
anticipated time required to hear from public speakers on any given or all agenda items, on the availability of Committee members
and the need to maintain quorum, and on any other relevant factor. The Committee shall not discuss or take action relative to any
general public comment except as explicitly permitted under the Brown Act.

COMMITTEE INFORMATION, ASSIGNMENTS, AND STRUCTURE

https://clerk.lacity.gov/clerk-services/cps/council-committee-meetings/info-assignments-structure

SPECIAL ACCOMMODATION
 Requests for reasonable modification or accommodation from individuals with disabilities, consistent with the Americans with
Disabilities Act, can be made by contacting the City Clerk's Office at (213) 978-1133. For Telecommunications Relay Service for the
hearing impaired, please see the information below.

NOTICE TO PAID REPRESENTATIVES

If a member of the public is compensated to monitor, attend, or speak at this meeting, City law may require them to register as a
lobbyist and report this activity. More information can be found at Los Angeles Municipal Code 48.01 et seq. or at
ethics.lacity.org/lobbying. Further assistance can be found by contacting the Ethics Commission at (213) 978-1960 or
ethics.commission@lacity.org.

EXHAUSTION OF ADMINISTRATIVE REMEDIES

A member of the public seeking to challenge a City action in court may be limited to raising only those issues raised at the public
hearing described in this notice, or in written correspondence delivered to the City Clerk prior to the public hearing in time reasonably
to be considered by the Committee members. Any written correspondence delivered to the City Clerk before the City Council's final
action on a matter will become a part of the administrative record.

TELECOMMUNICATIONS RELAY SERVICE (TRS) COMMUNICATIONS

Telephone communication is one of the most important forms of communication in society today. Due to advancements in
technology, telephone devices have evolved with new services and capabilities. Individuals who are deaf and hard of hearing, and
individuals with a speech disability, may be able to avail themselves of both for peer-to-peer and third-party telecommunications
relay service (TRS) communications. Telecommunications Relay Service is a telephone service that allows persons with hearing or
speech disabilities to place and receive telephone calls. TRS is available in all 50 states, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and
the U.S. territories for local and/or long distance calls. TRS providers - generally telephone companies - are compensated for the
costs of providing TRS from either a state or a federal fund. There is no cost to the TRS user.

What forms of TRS are available? There are several forms of TRS, depending on the particular needs of the user and the equipment
available: TRS includes: Text to Voice TIY-Based TRS; Speech-to-Speech Relay Service; Shared Non-English Language Relay
Service; Captioned Telephone Relay Service; Internet Protocol Relay Service; and Video Relay Service. Please visit this site for
detail descriptions, https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/telecommunications-relay-service-trs.

Don't hang up! Some people hang up on TRS calls because they think the caller is a telemarketer. If you hear, "Hello, this is the
relay service…" when you pick up the phone, please don't hang up! You are about to talk, through a TRS provider, to a person who
is deaf, hard-of-hearing, or has a speech disability.

For more information about FCC programs to promote access to telecommunications services for people with disabilities, visit the
FCC's Disability Rights Office website.

JOURNAL – SPECIAL BUDGET AND FINANCE ADVISORY COMMITTEE (BFAC) MEETING

  Friday, September 11, 2026

  ROOM 401, CITY HALL - 12:30 PM
  200 NORTH SPRING STREET, LOS ANGELES, CA 90012

  MEMBERS:  RON S. GALPERIN, CHAIR
  DERRIC J. JOHNSON, VICE CHAIR
  GILDA HAAS
  JOSEPH M. LUMARDA
  TOM DE SIMONE

  Armando Bencomo - Legislative Assistant - (213) 978-1080
  (or Clerk.BudgetandFinanceCommittee@lacity.org)

  Submit written comment at LACouncilComment.com

The audio for this meeting is broadcast live on the internet at https://clerk.lacity.gov/calendar. Additional information
regarding Committee procedures provided at the end of this agenda.

ITEM(S)

 (1)  Call to Order and Roll Call

  Members Present: Ron S. Galperin, Gilda Haas, Tom De Simone (3); Absent: Derric
  J. Johnson, Joseph M. Lumarda (2)

  Chairperson Galperin called the meeting to order at 12:37 p.m.

 (2)  Public Comment

  • Multiple Agenda Item Comment
  • General Public Comment

  The Committee provided an opportunity for Multiple Agenda Item Comments.
 (3)  City Asset Management Presentation
  Invited speakers from SOMOS Group will present recommendations
  for the management and development of City-owned land.

  Alfred Fraijo Jr., Founder and Chief Executive Officer, and Patricia Ortega Simo,
  Associate, of Somos Group provided an overview of a proposed nonprofit revitalization
  model consisting of a structured public-private partnership between the City and an
  independent nonprofit organization that could provide specialized asset development
  capacity and technical expertise for real estate and economic development initiatives
  and projects. Under the proposed model, the non-profit organization would coordinate
  the negotiation of comprehensive public-private partnerships, assemble and manage
  development sites, manage the activation of interim uses, support commercial corridors
  and economic revitalization, coordinate financing mechanisms and private sector
  investments, and manage the development processes for designated projects. The City
  would retain governmental and policy authority over land use, legal compliance, and
  taxation matters; approve project components, and establish development objectives
  through development agreements. The City would identify surplus assets for potential
  redevelopment or economic development, and make the appropriate determinations in
  compliance with applicable Surplus Land Act requirements. Such projects would be
  structured through development agreements, leases, disposition agreements, or any
  other applicable agreements. The nonprofit organization would perform the development
  and implemention functions assigned through the executed agreements to bring City-
  owned surplus assets to market for redevelopment.

  Development agreements would allow the City to designate the nonprofit organization to
  serve as a long-term development partner, and execute agreements that apply uniformly
  across multiple parcels within the designated overlays, while locking in negotiated public-
  private partnership terms and delivery obligations. Development agreements would vest
  the applicable zoning, General Plan, and land use regulations governing the project for
  the agreement term; and, can be amended to include additional sites as parcels become
  available without renegotiating the core development structure. The nonprofit
  organization could serve as a technical advisor for zoning changes and overlays that
  would allow for an expedited development process for surplus asset redevelopment
  projects, and issue streamlined Request for Proposals and Qualifications procedures in
  compliance with local and state law. The development agreements may also include
  revenue recycling provisions to subsidize future projects and support the use of technical
  experts for other projects.

  The Committee and SOMOS Group discussed the Surplus Land Act compliance process
  to be completed before the nonprofit organization would take stewardship over City-
  owned surplus assets, determining the highest value and best use of the surplus assets,
  designation of underutilized City-owned assets for the proposed revitalization model, and
  similar revitalization models implemented in other cities that successfully garnered
  stakeholder engagement, surrounding community support, and financial support.
 (4)  Staff Update
  Staff will share recent stakeholder engagement efforts and update on
  relevant City-wide policies.

  Charles Turner, Council District 5, provided an update on stakeholder engagement
  efforts, policy research conducted by BFAC staff, and recent legislative updates. UCLA
  Luskin Leadership Fellows Alberto Espiricueta, Hannah Klubeck, and Shaine Stuhlmuller
  have completed their acadamic term supporting the BFAC. Since the July 10, 2026
  BFAC Meeting, the ad hoc subcommittees and BFAC staff held meetings with internal
  City staff and external stakeholders across the City, and continued with outreach efforts
  to gather helpful feedback and engagement on the policy areas covered by the BFAC
  since November 2025. Chairperson Galperin and Member Lumarda met with
  representatives from various City department to discuss revenue-generating
  opportunities, including the Department of Recreation and Parks, Los Angeles City
  Employees’ Retirement System, and the Office of the City Administrative Officer. BFAC
  staff have supported internal and external discussions regarding real estate and asset
  management matters, and will continue to research issues related to the Surplus Land
  Act and the City’s asset management strategy. BFAC staff also met with representatives
  of the former Economic and Workforce Development Department (now consolidated into
  the Community Investment Department) to discuss the Comprehensive Economic
  Development Strategy (CEDS), which is a federally recognized planning process
  initiated by the Mayor’s Office as a prerequisite for the City’s designation as an
  Economic Development District by the U.S. Economic Development Administration. The
  CEDS team is currently in the outreach stage and will release the final plan for public
  review in June 2027.

  The City Council returned to its legislative session from Summer Recess on August 4,
  2026. During the August 4, 2026 Special Rules, Elections, and Intergovernmental
  Relations (REIR) Committee Meeting, the REIR Committee approved Motion (Harris-
  Dawson – Blumenfield) to establish a new Ad Hoc Committee on Charter Review [see
  Council File No. (CF) 24-2000-S4]. On August 18, 2026, the Budget and Finance
  Committee (BFC) discussed and approved the issuance and sale of Municipal
  Improvement Corporation of Los Angeles (MICLA) Lease Revenue Bonds for the Los
  Angeles Convention Center Expansion and Modernization Project (see CF 15-1207-
  S10). On August 26, 2026, the City Council adopted Motion (Blumenfield – McOsker) to
  re-activate and restore CF 11-1705 for consideration of a Los Angeles City Planning
  Commission report and proposed Ordinance relative to a comprehensive revision and
  consolidation of Citywide Sign Regulations into one section within the City’s Zoning
  Code for on-site and off-site signs. The Office of Finance has issued a report relative to
  the feasibility and fiscal impact of raising the threshold for the Small Business Tax
  Exemption (See CF 25-1474). The BFAC Progress Report No. 1 has been transmitted
  and referred to the BFC for consideration (see CF 25-0314), and the BFAC Progress
   Report No. 2 is being prepared. A BFAC representative will provide a presentation on the
  Progress Reports at a future BFC Meeting.

(5)  Policy Area Deliberation
  Committee members will deliberate and adopt a set of policy areas to
  move forward with crafting recommendations.

  The Committee and Charles Turner, Council District 5, discussed narrowing the scope
  for the development of the BFAC’s recommendations to the BFC. The four categories for
  the policy areas include revenue generation, funds management, better governance and
  savings, and leveraging City assets. Under the revenue generation category, the two
  policy areas under consideration include advertising on City-owned property and parking
  enforcement revenue. Under the funds management category, the three policy areas
  include long-term investment strategy, underutilized fund identification, and internal
  costs/internal Cost Allocation Plan (CAP). Under the better governance and savings
  category, the three policy areas include liability cost reduction, alternative dispute
  resolution/liability claims management, and Citywide auditing capacity. Under the
  leveraging City assets category, the two policy areas include real estate
  management/redevelopment strategy for the City, and advocacy around the Surplus
  Land Act.

  The policy area relative to advertising on City-owned property involves increased fines
  and penalties on Sign Code violations, setting up a registry for all off-site advertising
  companies to update their inventory, and other steps to ensure the City can enforce
  existing regulations with fines that can deter violations. The Committee may also look
  into identifying a potential pathway for the City to pursue revenue-generating
  opportunities from advertisements on City-owned property, such as fee-based digital
  signage and fee structures incorporated into development agreements. The policy area
  relative to parking enforcement revenue involves the development of recommendations
  to cover operational costs and restore some level of profitability, with the potential
  utilization of new technology, automation of parking tickets issued to delivery company
  vehicles, and the collection of parking violation fees from rental vehicles.

  The Committee will continue to evaluate the long-term investment strategy, investment
  rate of return, and the composition of the general investment pool within the City
  Treasury portfolio to realize any potential changes as a policy area within the fund
  management category. Other policy areas include better overall management of special
  funds through the establishment of a regular gathering of relevant parties and City
  departments to evaluate underutilized funds, establishing an internal CAP for
  compensation of general overhead costs charged to the General Fund, and evaluating
  the usage of issued bonds wherein the debt interest rate is higher than the City
  Treasury’s achieved investment rate of return.
   Regarding the policy area of liability cost reduction, the Committee will continue to focus
  on predictive analytics and utilizing geographic concentration data to address
  underserviced infrastructure and prioritize investments in identified areas. The alternative
  dispute resolution policy area to expeditiously mediate and resolve claims would involve
  the evaluation of claims data the existing Dispute Resolution Program administered by
  the City Attorney’s Office. The Committee is also exploring the Los Angeles Police
  Department’s ability to carry insurance for personnel with high levels of liability, such as
  tiered liability coverage based on performance and officer misconduct.

  Regarding the policy area of real estate management/redevelopment strategy to
  leverage assets, the Committee will continue to assess the underutilization and
  repurposing of City assets, and potential economic development opportunities that may
  result from the repurposed assets. The Committee agreed to remove Surplus Land
  advocacy as a policy area under consideration.

  The Committee discussed exploring additional policy areas, which include the potential
  implementation of a delivery fee for delivered packages and food, and the collection of
  personal business property tax by the County of Los Angeles. The Committee agreed to
  remove personal business tax as a prioritized policy area for consideration.

  After discussion on prioritizing the policy areas, Member De Simone move to adopt the
  set of policy areas as detailed above, which was seconded by Member Haas. The set of
  policy areas were adopted by the following vote: Ayes: Galperin, Haas, De Simone (3);
  Nays: (0); Absent: Johnson, Lumarda (2)

(6)  Approval of Minutes
  The Committee will review and approve the Minutes of the July 10,
  2026, Budget and Finance Advisory Committee meeting.

  Member De Simone moved to approve the Minutes of the July 10, 2026 Budget and
  Finance Advisory Committee Meeting, which was seconded by Member Haas – Ayes:
  Galperin, Haas, De Simone (3); Nays: (0); Absent: Johnson, Lumarda (2)

(7)  Next Steps and Calendar Review

  The next BFAC Meeting is scheduled on Friday, October 2, 2026 at 1:00 p.m. in City
  Hall.

(8)  Adjournment
   The Committee Meeting was adjourned at 3:08 p.m. with the following Members present:

  Present: Ron S. Galperin, Gilda Haas, Tom De Simone (3); Absent: Derric J.
  Johnson, Joseph M. Lumarda (2)
